messages:
Sam (AcmeOps): Hey team — starting ~10:12 UTC we're seeing a bunch of 504s from Redwood hosted inference. Happens across multiple endpoints. SDK clients show repeated retries and a bunch of `401`/`429` around the same time. Can we triage?
Maya (support): Sorry about that, Sam. Can you paste a short log sample and what SDK version you're on? Also confirmed for the rest of the team: customer reports 504s and auth failures, likely contributing to retries.
Sam (AcmeOps): SDK v1.8.2 via npm. Snippet from our client (timestamps redacted):
```
[10:12:01] request -> /v1/generate 200ms
[10:12:02] auth: refresh token start
[10:12:02] auth: refresh token -> 429 Too Many Requests
[10:12:02] sdk: retrying request (attempt 1)
[10:12:03] request -> /v1/generate 504 Gateway Timeout
[10:12:03] auth: refresh token -> 429 Too Many Requests
[10:12:03] sdk: retrying request (attempt 2)
[10:12:04] request -> /v1/generate 504 Gateway Timeout
```
Sam (AcmeOps): We also see token refresh spike when many new client processes start after a deploy — looks like all clients hit auth at once.
sre-alert-bot: [ALERT] 504 spike on hosted-api:region-us-east-1 at 10:12 UTC — 120s average 504s rising above threshold.
Maya (support): Thanks, that matches other small reports. I'm escalating to runtime and SRE to check gateway/backends and auth rate limits. Liam / Jess, can you pick this up?
Liam (eng-runtime): Jumping in. From the logs it looks like token refreshes are returning 429 which then leads the SDK to immediately retry requests without backoff, causing large transient load hitting gateway and backend inference pods. Two suspicion paths: 1) auth service rate-limit for token refresh (per key) triggered by many clients doing refresh at the same time; 2) SDK's retry/backoff behavior not honoring jitter/exponential backoff for auth errors.
Jess (eng-sre): On SRE side I can see a short spike of incoming connections correlating with the timestamp. Gateway CPU climbed to ~85% for a minute and a few backend pods reported increased queue length. No sustained error in infra but transient overload plausible. Also seeing elevated 429s from auth-service.
Liam (eng-runtime): Repro steps I used locally to mimic: spin up 50 parallel processes calling `client.refreshToken()` then immediately fire generation requests. Repro shows auth returning 429 for ~30% of refreshes and subsequent 504s from gateway. Repro commands:
```
# quick repro (Linux)
for i in {1..50}; do node -e "const c=require('./client'); c.refreshAndCall()" & done
# client code does: refresh -> generate in quick succession
```
Liam (eng-runtime): Root cause hypothesis: token refreshes are throttled per-key per-minute; SDK does not cache token aggressively for short-lived clients and retries too aggressively on 429/401. That causes thundering herd on auth and then overloaded gateway/backends which return 504s.
Andrew (support-mgr): Action items: 1) Triage and temporary mitigations for customer; 2) Short-term infra/workaround; 3) SDK hotfix for safer backoff and caching.
Maya (support): Sam — immediate mitigation options: a) roll forward process so clients reuse existing token rather than refresh on startup, b) set SDK env override to increase token cache TTL (SDK_TOKEN_CACHE_TTL=300) if possible, c) stagger startup of clients. Can you try (b) and report?
Sam (AcmeOps): Will try TTL override now and report in ~5m. Also curious if Redwood can temporarily increase auth rate limit for our key while we push a patch.
Jess (eng-sre): I can request a short-term rate-limit bump for Sam's API key for the next 30 minutes to reduce 429s — will do that now. Notifying infra: `@infra` (internal).
sre-alert-bot: [INFO] rate-limit override applied for key: acct-acmeops-*** for 30m by eng-sre.
Maya (support): Heads-up: we applied a temporary increase for Sam while SRE/infra monitors. Sam, please try the SDK env change.
Sam (AcmeOps): OK set `SDK_TOKEN_CACHE_TTL=300` and restarted clients. Initial 5 minutes look much better — almost no 429s and requests succeeding. Will monitor for another 10m.
Liam (eng-runtime): Good verification. Longer-term fixes we plan: - SDK v1.8.3 patch to add exponential backoff + jitter for auth failures and make token cache TTL a configurable option with better defaults. - Add server-side guidance and docs about token refresh best practices. - Consider auth-service smoothing for short bursts or small token-grant queue.
Maya (support): ETA on SDK hotfix?
Liam (eng-runtime): I'll cut a patch branch today and aim for a canary release to npm in ~6 hours (v1.8.3-canary). Full stable release in 24-48h pending tests. Will post the canary npm tag and changelog here.
Liam (eng-runtime): Canary notes: changed retry logic to handle 4xx auth codes differently (no immediate request retry; refresh attempts follow exponential backoff up to 5 attempts with jitter). Also added default token cache TTL=120s (configurable).
Jess (eng-sre): On infra, we'll keep the temporary rate-limit bump in place for 30m and monitor. If traffic remains high from many customers we may throttle by ip-range rather than key to avoid repeated per-key escalations.
Sam (AcmeOps): Thanks all — so far stable after TTL bump and rate-limit bump. Appreciate the quick support.
Maya (support): Great. I'll post a customer-facing summary and the suggested SDK env workaround. Sam, can we follow up after 24h for retrospective?
Sam (AcmeOps): Yes happy to.
Liam (eng-runtime): Posting quick repro & patch link once I push canary: npm tag `redwood-sdk@1.8.3-canary.1` and link in thread.
Liam (eng-runtime): [later] Published canary: `npm i redwood-sdk@1.8.3-canary.1` — includes backoff + token TTL config.
Andrew (support-mgr): Thanks team. I'll draft the internal postmortem after incident cool-down. Marking this thread for follow-up in 24h to confirm SDK release and stabilization.
Maya (support): Sam — final note for your team: recommended steps: 1) keep `SDK_TOKEN_CACHE_TTL=300` until you upgrade to 1.8.3, 2) stagger process startups if possible, 3) upgrade to canary when convenient and then stable release.
Sam (AcmeOps): Will keep TTL for now and plan upgrade. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
Liam (eng-runtime): Closing loop here after stable release. If anything recurs ping this thread and we'll reopen.
